findings.evidence: Definition at line 296 quantifies only over mass-shell pairs and asserts the `F t • (p+p')` shape; `IsCovariant` (120) quantifies over `IsElasticStabilizer g p p' f`, i.e. maps fixing *these* `p, p'`, so it cannot constrain `J` at another transition. The module docstring itself concedes the gap at lines 62-65 ("it is not proved here, and `HasFormFactor` carries it as part of what it asserts"), while lines 14-18 claim the file "proves ... = F(t) (p + p')^μ". Roadmap §3.1 (README.md:699-701) requires proving that covariance and conservation "leave exactly one scalar function of the invariant momentum transfer".
findings.fix: Introduce family covariance as above plus an explicitly named hypothesis that the isometries act transitively on equal-mass transitions with equal `t` (the Witt-type step, which is not in Mathlib — `docs/1000.yaml:4007` lists Witt's theorem with no declaration), and derive the existence of `F` with `HasFormFactor` from that hypothesis together with `IsCovariant.existsUnique_eq_smul`. Short of that, keep `HasFormFactor` but state in its own docstring (not only in the module header) that it assumes the t-dependence, and reword the module headline at line 16 so the `F(t)` form is not advertised as proved.
findings.issue: `HasFormFactor g m2 J F := ∀ p p', g p p = m2 → g p' p' = m2 → J p p' = F (g (p'-p) (p'-p)) • (p+p')` asserts the very thing §3.1 asks to be proved: that the coefficient is a function of t alone. Covariance here is only stabiliser invariance at one fixed transition (`IsCovariant`, line 120), so nothing in the file relates coefficients at two different transitions with equal t; the file never defines covariance for a family (`∀ f isometry, f (J p p') = J (f p) (f p')`), which is the notion the missing transitivity step would consume. Consequently all of `HasFormFactor.isCovariant` (314), `apply_sub_eq_zero` (320), `apply_eq_of_hasFormFactor` (327) and `apply_zero_eq` (336) — the last being the roadmap's charge-normalisation milestone — follow from the assumed shape, not from the physics: `apply_zero_eq` just reads off `F 0 • (p+p) = 2e • p`.

findings.evidence: Line 175: `∃ a b : ℝ, J = a • p + b • p'`; line 188: `∃ A B : ℝ, J = A • (p + p') + B • (p' - p)`.
findings.issue: The module docstring attributes the sum/difference decomposition to `FormFactor.IsCovariant.exists_eq_smul_add_smul`, which actually yields `J = a • p + b • p'` (line 173-175). The sum/difference statement is `IsCovariant.exists_eq_smul_add_add_smul_sub` (line 186).

summary: The pointwise result (covariance + conservation + equal mass ⇒ a unique multiple of p+p') is correctly stated and genuinely proved, and the single-pole arithmetic, witness transition and charge-radius convention all check out. But the part of the §3.1 target that makes F a form factor — that the coefficient depends on the transition only through t — is folded into the definition `HasFormFactor` rather than derived, so the module's headline claim and every `HasFormFactor.*` lemma are consequences of that assumption, not of covariance and conservation.
